speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms of vomiting and chest pain, including when they started and if they radiate to your arm, jaw, or back. Also, let me know if you have any history of heart disease or recent trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture). The patient's presentation of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption, followed by severe chest pain and choking, is the classic triad for esophageal rupture. Given the potential for mediastinitis, I am immediately requesting a CT scan of the chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
